# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**RE: Appeal of Denial – Reference Number POC-92D596C7F2-83353**
**Member:** Jordan Hayes
**Member ID:** W671447302
**Plan:** MedStar Family Choice DC (Commercial/ACA), District of Columbia
**Date of Denial Notice:** August 3, 2026
**Requested Service:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
**Governing Policy:** Utilization Management Criteria — https://www.medstarfamilychoicedc.com/-/media/project/mho/mfcdc/medical-policies-and-procedures/policy-115dc_utilization-management-criteria.pdf

Dear MedStar Family Choice DC Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my request for lower back disc surgery / decompression (CPT 63030). My denial notice, dated August 3, 2026, states that the request was denied because "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I am asking the plan to reconsider this decision. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and the records already in the plan's possession describe my condition and treatment history in detail.

## The Documentation in My Records

The prior authorization packet submitted by my care team includes the following, which I ask the plan to review again in full:

- **Duration and nature of symptoms:** 18 months of progressive lower back pain, unrelieved by rest.
- **Conservative treatment already completed:** Supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, over 8 weeks (April 14, 2026 – June 9, 2026), with 16 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trial:** NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on April 29, 2026, which gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging:** MRI of the lumbar spine on June 16, 2026, showing an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.
- **Functional limitation:** I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes, and I have radicular pain into my right calf.
- **Physical exam findings:** Positive provocative testing on the affected side, with a neurologic deficit that corresponds to the level shown on imaging.
- **Absence of contraindications:** No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI of 29, non-smoker.

Given this record, I am asking the plan to identify specifically what documentation it considers incomplete, since the notice does not say.

## The Plan's Own Policy on Criteria

The plan's Utilization Management Criteria policy states: "MedStar Family Choice DC follows documented UM criteria to facilitate consistency in UM decision making across all service types." It also states: "All criteria utilized in utilization management are available upon request." The policy further states: "The following criteria and processes, as documented on MedStar Family Choice DC web site, are utilized for UM decision making:" and that decisions are "based on the following criteria," followed by a listing of criteria sources.

I have not been given the actual clinical criteria that were applied to my specific request — only the plan's general statement that such criteria exist and are available on request. I say this plainly so the reviewer understands: **nothing in the material I have received quotes the specific clinical standard used to evaluate CPT 63030 in my case.** I am not able to compare my records against criteria I have not seen.

## Request for the Specific Criteria Applied

I understand my plan may use InterQual criteria, which is licensed software rather than a public document. I am nonetheless entitled to see it. Federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules require the plan to give me, free of charge, the specific rule or criterion relied on for this denial. I am formally requesting, in writing, **the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination** — or, if some other criteria set was used, the specific criteria document and section applied to CPT 63030 in my case. The plan's own policy confirms that "[p]roviders may request the UM criteria for UM decision making," and I am asking that the same information be provided to me as the member.

## What I Am Asking For

1. That the plan reconsider the denial of CPT 63030 in light of the clinical documentation summarized above.
2. That the plan identify, specifically, what documentation was considered incomplete, so that my care team can supply it if it exists.
3. That the plan provide, in writing, the specific criteria — including the InterQual subset and edition, if applicable — that were applied to my request.

I understand my appeal must be received by **January 30, 2027** (180 days from the date of the denial notice). I am submitting this appeal to the address printed on my denial letter. If that address is not clear, I will call the number on the back of my insurance card to confirm where member appeals are filed.

Thank you for reconsidering my request. Please contact me if you need any additional information.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Jordan Hayes
Member ID: W671447302
Date: [DATE OF SIGNATURE]
Address: [MEMBER ADDRESS]
Phone: [MEMBER PHONE NUMBER]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
